chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Sinan, who said: A man from the people of Hamadan, called Abdullah ibn al-Dhahhak, narrated to me from Abu Khalid al-Ahmar from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, who said:

Rasulullah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Certainly, when the orphan cries, the Throne shakes for him, so the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, says: Who is it that made My servant cry, whose parents I took during his childhood? By My might and majesty, no one will comfort him except that I will make Paradise obligatory for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for comforting a crying orphan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, this hadith emphasizes the cosmic weight of an orphan’s grief, depicting the Divine Throne (*al-‘Arsh*) trembling in empathy. It establishes a direct divine guarantee of Paradise for those who soothe the orphan, linking the act of *tadkhīr* (consolation) to the alleviation of the specific sorrow caused by early parental loss.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Sinan, from a man from the people of Hamadan named Abdullah ibn al-Dhahhak, from Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari that

Rasulullah (sw) said: Certainly, when the orphan cries, the Divine Throne starts to shakes for him, then the Lord Almighty says: "Who is it that made My servant cry, of whose parents I have taken during his childhood? By My might and majesty, no one will comfort him except that I will make Paradise obligatory for him."
